toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The departures are concentrated in one place. Eight of the 11 associates assigned to Kestrel have resigned, against 1 of the 13 who never worked on it. Other groups are at normal attrition, so the firm-wide hours increase and general market mobility don't explain this group. A group-wide pay gap doesn't fit either: the 13 associates not on Kestrel were paid the same and nearly all stayed. I'm fairly confident about that.

I can't yet separate two explanations. Kestrel's workload and its only supervising partner, Dorian Faulk, are completely overlapping. All 11 Kestrel associates reported to him, and he supervises no one else. Survey comments mention both relentless weekends and humiliating late-night corrections. Fixing the wrong one wastes money and could blame the wrong person.

Don't announce the £12k payment and close the review. It targets the least-supported explanation and ends the inquiry. Do the confidential outside interviews (about £9k, three weeks), structured to separate supervision from workload. Four leavers have already agreed. Meanwhile, add matter and supervising-partner fields to attrition reporting. Choose between contract reviewers and a change of supervisor after the interviews. Overall confidence is moderate.
